tanque-verde-ridge.note: Saguaro National Park's conditions page, last updated September 9, 2026 (the most recent official update available; reconfirmed today with no newer NPS update posted), confirms all trails within the Rincon Mountain District (East) are open, including this trail, which was previously closed in June 2026 due to the Box Fire before the fire reached full containment and closures were lifted by June 16, 2026 (Source: National Park Service). No NWS Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning is active anywhere in Arizona today, confirmed via a live check of the National Weather Service active alerts feed at api.weather.gov (Source: National Weather Service). Hike before 7am or after 7pm and carry extra water given continued summer heat.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: No change since the National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page was reconfirmed today via a direct live fetch, still last updated September 24, 2026: South Kaibab Trail is open only from the trailhead to Tip-Off Point, about 4.4 miles down, and closed below that due to hazardous conditions from flash flooding (Source: National Park Service). Ooh Aah Point (0.9 miles) and Cedar Ridge (1.5 miles), the trail's popular shorter destinations, remain within the open section. Recovery from the flash flooding in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, 2026 that damaged water intake infrastructure continues, with no estimated reopening posted for the closed section below Tip-Off. Corridor water remains off at all listed points, including South Kaibab Trailhead, to conserve water; hikers should carry sufficient water or be prepared to treat water from natural sources. This trail is fully sun exposed with no reliable water source below the trailhead. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning is active anywhere in Arizona today, confirmed via a live check of the National Weather Service active alerts feed at api.weather.gov (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: No change since the National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page was reconfirmed today via a direct live fetch, still last updated September 24, 2026: Bright Angel Trail is open from the trailhead down to River Resthouse; the Plateau Point Trail is also open. The trail remains closed below River Resthouse; the River Trail segment east of River Resthouse to the South Kaibab Trail junction is also closed (Source: National Park Service). Corridor water remains off at every listed point, including Havasupai Gardens, Bright Angel Trailhead, Three-Mile Resthouse, and Mile-and-a-Half Resthouse, to conserve water; hikers should carry sufficient water or be prepared to treat water from natural sources. No estimated reopening is posted for sections below River Resthouse. Confirm current conditions with the Backcountry Information Center at 928-638-7875 before descending past Havasupai Gardens. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning is active anywhere in Arizona today, confirmed via a live check of the National Weather Service active alerts feed at api.weather.gov (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.

rim-trail.note: No closures are posted today; the Rim Trail does not appear anywhere in the current or closed sections of the National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page, reconfirmed today via a direct live fetch, still last updated September 24, 2026, and is not affected by the Bright Angel Canyon flash flood closures (Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park). No NWS Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning is active anywhere in Arizona today, confirmed via a live check of the National Weather Service active alerts feed at api.weather.gov (Source: National Weather Service). Use caution near the rim during any lightning.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, from the North Kaibab Trailhead to Phantom Ranch, including Cottonwood Campground, remains closed with no estimated reopening, reconfirmed today on the National Park Service's Key Hiking Messages page via a direct live fetch, still last updated September 24, 2026, following significant flash flooding in Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, 2026 (Source: National Park Service). Phantom Ranch, Bright Angel Campground, the Canteen, and cabins remain fully closed, as do the Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings and Boat Beach. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning, Heat Advisory, or Red Flag Warning is active anywhere in Arizona today, confirmed via a live check of the National Weather Service active alerts feed at api.weather.gov (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
